messages:
alex: Thinking out loud — proposal to add a throttle matrix to the console so teams can set endpoint-specific limits (chat, embeddings, rerank, streaming) per-org and optionally per-key. would make burst handling explicit.

maria: Nice. do you mean separate token-buckets for each endpoint type? or a single bucket with weights?

alex: Prefer separate buckets. streaming has different latency/cost profile so mixing it causes noisy neighbors. also want an admin-facing fallback policy if a bucket is exceeded (soft-limit vs hard 429).

jamal: operational concern: enforcement path matters. if we do per-key + per-org we risk double counting if enforcement lives in both api-gateway and backend. need idempotent checks or a single authoritative check.

kevin: agree. simplest is authoritative check at edge (kong/nginx layer) + token-metadata passed through. fallback check in runtime for safety (not counting towards quota again). can use a header like X-Quota-Consumed to avoid double-charge.

sophie: UX q: how should console expose this? matrix grid (rows=endpoints, cols=mode: rate/burst/fallback) or policy DSL? customers want simple toggles + an advanced JSON editor.

maria: grid + quick presets (dev, prod, enterprise) would be ideal. presets can map to sensible bursts for streaming (low) vs embeddings (higher).

alex: draft enforcement config example: 
```json
{
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "quotas": {
    "chat": { "rate_rps": 50, "burst": 400, "fallback": "queue:30s" },
    "embeddings": { "rate_rps": 20, "burst": 1000, "fallback": "throttle" },
    "rerank": { "rate_rps": 10, "burst": 200, "fallback": "429" },
    "streaming": { "rate_rps": 5, "burst": 40, "fallback": "graceful-degrade" }
  },
  "per_key_override": true
}
```

jamal: two notes: (1) "queue:30s" needs a queue-length cap and memory bounds; (2) streaming fallback should prefer a degraded streaming mode (lower chunk freq) not full block.

kevin: telemetry: we should emit per-endpoint token consumption, enforcement decision (allowed/throttled/fallback_taken), and latency impact. add labels: endpoint, model, policy_id. these need to map to dashboards and Alerting thresholds.

sophie: for rollout UX — expose an A/B canary for quota changes: e.g., increase burst for 10% of traffic for 24h, then auto-promote. "preview" mode that shows what would have been throttled in the last 7 days (dry-run).

maria: API design question: should the admin API accept the matrix as a single PATCH to /orgs/:id/quotas or per-endpoint PATCHs? atomicity matters. admin console will want a single save button.

alex: single PATCH server-side that validates and applies with a versioned policy object. per-endpoint PATCH can be a convenience wrapper in SDKs.

quota-bot: INFO: current defaults applied to org_123: chat rate=30rps burst=200, embeddings rate=15rps burst=500, streaming rate=3rps burst=20. No per-key overrides found.

jamal: next steps: kevin to sketch enforcement flow and headers, sophie to mock console grid + canary UX, alex to PR a policy schema and validation rules, maria to write product note for sales/CS.

sophie: i'll add previews for "would-be-throttled" view, want to include sample customer personas in the mock. :+1:

alex: thanks all — will open RFC and tag this thread. :rocket:
